### manynames3/sovereign-source-mvp

- Exact commit / revision: `ef177edbfae3a43e5a7ad7d9e53953ad5868f5b7`
- Date inspected: 2026-09-19
- Status: watch / clean-room only
- What it contains: Zero-star defense/aerospace supplier-qualification and controlled-RFQ workflow with deterministic facility matching, hard blockers, explainable reasons, evidence states, secure invite/access gates and a real starter-supplier pipeline joining DoD USAspending awards to optional SAM public extracts by UEI.
- Rare or undernoticed value: The useful product pattern is evidence-gated sourcing rather than another vendor directory. Unknown classification, missing buyer approval, facility/process/material/tolerance/quantity/inspection mismatch and missing/expired compliance evidence can block a match or force manual review. The public-data pipeline deliberately leaves NADCAP/CMMC as `VERIFY` states instead of fabricating status from inaccessible systems.
- Likely buyer / user: Defense, aerospace, naval and precision-manufacturing procurement teams; primes and supplier-development teams qualifying facilities before releasing controlled RFQs.
- Painful problem: Buyer teams waste RFQ cycles and create control risk when supplier capability, facility evidence and release authorization are spread across spreadsheets, public registries and manual review.
- Monetization mechanism / first paid wedge: Fixed-price supplier-qualification/RFQ-readiness pilot using public USAspending/SAM evidence plus customer-supplied qualification records; later recurring evidence-expiry and routing workflow.
- Build-time / data advantage: Roughly 2-4 months of domain/workflow discovery for facility-level qualification, evidence-state handling, deterministic match reasons and USAspending-to-SAM starter data.
- Concrete evidence inspected: Exact commit/tree; `README.md`; `sovereign_starter_db.py` with USAspending pagination, UEI dedupe, chunked pipe-delimited SAM extract processing, active-registration filtering, exact UEI join and SQLite indexes; `src/lib/matching.ts` with explicit hard blockers/manual-review states and deterministic capability/evidence scoring.
- License / rights: No repository-wide license was established at the inspected revision. Public visibility is not a reuse grant.
- Reuse classification: Inspect/learn/clean-room only unless permission or an explicit license is established. Public government-source data terms and authorized-access boundaries remain separate.
- Why it is not already obvious / crowded: Zero stars and a sourcing-MVP presentation hide a fairly mature evidence-gating state machine and a lawful public-data supplier pipeline.
- Score: **23/30** — A4 speed to revenue; B5 ACV/ceiling; C5 build/domain compression; D4 workflow advantage; E4 implementation evidence; F1 rights/reuse clarity.
- Combination opportunities: CaptureBrief opportunity/award intelligence + DATA Act identity semantics + this facility/evidence gate can produce a stronger supplier/teaming qualification packet; pair with CivicProof-style evidence acceptance so every eligibility reason has traceable support.
- Next action: Clean-room only the acceptance contract: unknown classification or unverified required evidence cannot become `ELIGIBLE`; benchmark it on 20 synthetic/public supplier packages with expired/missing/conflicting evidence.

### GSA/open-gsa-redesign — Subcontracting Plan Reports API
- URL: https://github.com/GSA/open-gsa-redesign
- Exact commit / revision: `494b1312e9c6436474840befe6e1964da15932b3`
- Date inspected: 2026-09-19
- Status: strong / Master contender
- What it contains: Official GSA SAM.gov OpenAPI 3.1 schema for the modernized eSRS Subcontracting Plan Reports API. Search fields include exact UEI, ultimate-parent UEI, legal business name, PIID, referenced-IDV PIID, subcontract number, organization code, fiscal year/report type and reporting period; response sections cover report, entity, contract, task-order, goals/actuals and certification data, with optional remarks/DoD attachments.
- Rare or undernoticed value: This is an official schema for subcontracting-plan performance evidence that can sit beside award/incumbent history. It exposes contract lineage and small-business-goal/actual reporting context that generic SAM/USAspending opportunity tools usually omit.
- Likely buyer / user: GovCon capture/BD teams, primes, subcontractors, supplier-diversity/compliance groups and consultants analyzing incumbent/team performance.
- Painful problem: Award history alone does not tell a capture team how a prime reports subcontracting goals/actuals or tie those reports cleanly to PIID/referenced-IDV/UEI lineage.
- Monetization mechanism / first paid wedge: Add an authorized `incumbent subcontracting evidence` section to CaptureBrief qualification packets for customers that already have the required SAM.gov System Account access.
- Build-time / data advantage: Roughly 2-4 months of official schema/access/field semantics and contract-lineage discovery avoided.
- Concrete evidence inspected: Exact revision; `_apidocs/spr-api/v1/openapi.yaml` with API title/version, RBAC/System Account security, UEI/ultimate-parent UEI/PIID/referenced-IDV filters, report/contract/entity/task-order/goals-and-actuals/certification schemas and attachment behavior; repository license/public-domain notice.
- License / rights: Official U.S. government work; repository licensing states U.S. government/public-domain treatment domestically with CC0 availability for worldwide reuse. Actual report access is permissioned and requires authorized System Account credentials/API key.
- Reuse classification: Schema/documentation can be reused under stated rights; production data access must remain within authorized SAM.gov permissions. Do not portray this as an anonymous public endpoint.
- Why it is not already obvious / crowded: The valuable schema is buried inside a broad GSA redesign repository and is not surfaced by generic SAM API searches.
- Score: **29/30** — A4 speed to revenue; B5 ACV/ceiling; C5 build/domain compression; D5 rare official evidence; E5 completeness; F5 rights clarity.
- Combination opportunities: DATA Act UEI/parent semantics + USAspending award history + SPR PIID/referenced-IDV and goals/actuals + mcp-sam-gov clause/deviation evidence can create a materially richer incumbent/team diligence packet.
- Next action: Add an optional SPR evidence contract to the 10-live-solicitation benchmark and test only with authorized access; require explicit unresolved state when a customer lacks SPR permission.

### bedrocka-ventures/bedrocka-tools-calc
- URL: https://github.com/bedrocka-ventures/bedrocka-tools-calc
- Exact commit / revision: `7723112b433f6ca9351bddaf0c37248e673356db`
- Date inspected: 2026-09-19
- Status: rejected / unsafe as current GovCon eligibility authority
- What it contains: MIT deterministic SBA size-standard calculator/checker.
- Why rejected: Its inspected federal-contracting receipts logic uses a three-year average and expects user-supplied size thresholds. Current 13 CFR §121.104 generally uses the most recent five completed fiscal years for concerns in business five or more years, with program-specific exceptions, and affiliate receipts matter. A stale deterministic rule is more dangerous than an explicit unresolved state.
- License / rights: MIT, but licensing does not fix legal-rule staleness.
- Value score: **15/30** — A2, B3, C3, D2, E3, F2 for safe present reuse.
- Next action: Do not use its eligibility result path. Prefer a versioned official SBA/eCFR reference artifact with rule effective dates and explicit exception/affiliation handling.
